title.narrative: Number of death sentences handed out in China

description.narrative: Number of death sentences handed out in China

comment.narrative: There is as yet no official data on the number of death penalties carried out in China and the figure remains a state secret. Amnesty International estimates annual death penalty figures are in the several thousands Death Sentences and Executions 2018 report April 2019. Both GBCCs sources partners and Amnesty International estimate that the majority of cases carrying the death penalty involve murder and drug related offenses.
The abolishment of the death penalty in China is a longterm goal. Within the 3year timeframe of the project we aim for a reduction and restriction on the application of the death penalty in practice.

description.narrative: R3.8 By 2020, new training module prepared by International and Chinese experts is completed, building on previous EIDHR and UK funded work;R3.9 A professional networking and mentoring scheme established for criminal defence lawyers in China and Europe (50 lawyers);R3.10 Two TOT training sessions for 12 lawyers and 8 lawyers delivered in Beijing by International and Chinese experts; R3.11Training session with cohort of 100 trained judicial stakeholders and legal professionals in Dali, combining theory and practice;R3.12. Capacity building activities for legal aid centres handling drugs death penalty cases in Dali, targeting 100 lawyers;R3.13 Experience sharing seminar in Beijing for 80 legal practitioners from other provinces is completed.

comment.narrative: Lack of legal practitioners awareness of the complexities of drug cases carrying the death penalty and ability how to deal with these. More so in the case of legal aid lawyers. Professor Wus team will run a one year project specifically looking to develop mechanisms to measure the quality of legal aid service provided by legal aid lawyers in death penalty cases and increase their capacity through training.

Between 20192022 Comparison of number of successful pilot cases with baseline confirm increase in the quality of lawyers and legal aid lawyers. NILA research demonstrates a qualitative improvement in judges and lawyers and capacity sentencing policy or defence strategy at first instance and SPC Review stage.
